fixtureFiles.README.md: Java 25 project. These are partial fixtures for a design/review task, not a complete build. A producer thread calls emit serially. Only the aliases shown are retained. The worker's recorder reads the payload synchronously and does not retain it afterward. Review production selection, not only the inline test sink.
fixtureFiles.docs/thread-safety-review.md:
# Proposed optimization
Replace queue.put(record.clone()) with queue.put(record) in QueuedSink.submit.
ArrayBlockingQueue is thread-safe, so the proposal assumes the record contents remain safe.
No change to Producer, production configuration, recorder or externally visible behavior is proposed.

Required contract: a successful submission must later record the byte value supplied for that
submission, in queue order. It does not mean recording has already completed. Each source array is
stable while submit executes; any access afterward follows the configured producer's code. No other
aliases are retained. Preserve the selected producer policy. Do not claim an allocation/throughput
gain without measurement.

requiredEvidence: Follows production configuration to QueuedSink and the reuse branch in Producer, rather than relying on InlineSink's existing test.
Recognizes queue insertion publication applies to preceding writes and does not freeze the retained scratch array.
Identifies that the consumer's delayed recorder reads are the relevant observation, not put/take success.
evaluator.expectedOutcome: Reject removal of the stable copy under this unchanged producer policy, or identify an alternative protocol that preserves every accepted record without silently altering caller obligations. Retaining the current clone is a sufficient scoped choice because the source is guaranteed stable during submit.
requiredValidation: Delay recorder read until after a second emit reuses scratch; the first queued record must still be 7, not 9.
Observe recorded values rather than queue size or method success.
Keep insertion/consumer-completion and rejected/interrupted-submission ownership explicit where relevant.
failureConditions: Approves original-array publication solely from ArrayBlockingQueue thread safety or its happens-before guarantee.
Offers volatile on the reference or producer-only locking as sufficient payload protection.
Relies on the synchronous inline test as proof for queued production behavior.
Calls the copied container deeply immutable without its element/ownership conditions.
evaluator.observableArtifact: Updated review states why the clone is needed for the configured producer and gives a consumer-content counterexample/validation schedule.

evaluator.changedConstraint: Only producer.storage changes from reuse to transfer. The same source allocates a fresh array for each emit and retains no other alias under the supplied fixture contract. Everything else is identical.
requiredEvidence: Reads the changed production selection and fresh-array branch.
Establishes that producer access ends on successful handoff, the receiver is the sole remaining user and recorder does not retain callbacks/aliases.
Uses the queue's publication contract for preceding initialization, without misclassifying the mutable array as immutable.
evaluator.expectedOutcome: Recognize that original-array handoff can preserve the required contents under proven exclusive ownership; the clone or an added lock is not required for this contract. Document the conditional caller obligation and what evidence would invalidate it. A retained copy can be a stated optional tradeoff, not asserted as a concurrency necessity.
requiredValidation: Exercise delayed consumer access across multiple emits and confirm each accepted value remains distinct.
If reuse or pooling is introduced later, require its completion/ownership evidence before reusing this conclusion.
Do not claim measured speed/allocation improvement from this review alone.
failureConditions: Treats all mutable publication as unsafe even with the specified exclusive transfer and queue memory edge.
Requires a new lock/copy without identifying an unsatisfied invariant.
Claims queue removal proves processing complete or permits producer reuse while the recorder still reads.
Ignores the changed selector and repeats case 1's required-copy conclusion.
